newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 16.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - Ceska Pojistovna said it sold its 36 percent share in the largest Czech cable telvision operator, Kabel plus to U.S. West.
PRAVO - The congressional court in Brno decided to allow three high profile candidates to run for Senate, overturning decisions from the Central Election committee and the High Court.

- The government is not considering any administrative steps to limit imports or to devalue the crown, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated after a Tuesday meeting with economic ministers to discuss the growing trade deficit.

- The Doctor's Trade Union Club will decide on October 24th whether or not to hold a strike for changes to the healthcare system and higher wages for doctors according to David Rath, the club's chairman.
- Ceska Rafinerska a.s., the main domestic fuel producer, posted gross profits of 700 million crowns in the first nine months of this year according to the company's general manager, Ivan Ottis.

- If Ceske Drahy does not take steps to stop the planned decrease of employees, the rail company will not be able to ensure quality service in the future according to Jaromir Dusek, the chairman of the Railway Workers Trade Union.

- Shareholders of Letov Praha a.s. decided to restructure the aviation company on condition that the Czech government supports the aviation industry and that Letov receives a loaqn for approximately 60 million crowns.
- The average household income in the first half of this year was 12,786 crowns, or 5135 crowns per member.
- Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka is a new shareholder in the Penzijni Fond Energie with ten percent of the shares.

- If a state subsidy and support program is not announced for Aero Vodochody, the company's board will be forced to request a public tender. Aero Vodochody is the largest manufacturer of training aircraft.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Agrobanka, which is currently under forced administration from the Czech National Bank, is to receive a two billion crown loan from Germany's Commerzbank according to the chairman of Commerzbank's board of directors, Martin Kohlhaussen.

- Citibank, which obtained the award for the best foreign bank in the Czech Republic from Euromoney magazine, posted a net profit of 137.9 million crowns in the first half year. The bank is currently considering opening a series of branch offices in major industrial cities.
- Creditanstalt, a 100-percent daughter company of the leading Austrian bank, Creditanstalt-Bankverein, has received a license for supplying mortgages.
